conclusion: For the output SMEM state path, the candidate now creates a managed device link to the qcom_smp2p supplier before acquiring the state handle. Its .remove callback clears and puts that handle under the same mutex used across qcom_smem_state_update_bits(), so managed supplier unbind orders consumer teardown before provider removal. This is supported by pinned-kernel source and a reproducible Docker build; it is not runtime-verified or stock-exact.

findings.description: The qcom,smem-states property is absent from the pinned kernel of_supplier_bindings table. The output probe resolves the state child node to its parent qcom_smp2p platform device and adds a managed DL_FLAG_AUTOREMOVE_CONSUMER link before qcom_smem_state_get(). The .remove callback nulls the handle, clears shadow/cursor state, and puts the handle while holding rdbg_smem_state_lock. rdbg_write holds this same lock across the provider callback, so remove waits for an in-flight update.

The new .remove callback handles the output SMEM state only. An open character-device file may retain a requested input IRQ; input IRQ/domain teardown and concurrent open-file operations across provider unbind are not yet drained or verified.

limitations: This change addresses the output SMEM provider callback lifetime only.
Input IRQ, active file descriptors, and operations across unbind/rebind remain unverified.
